title: The Periodic Table: Order from Atomic Number

questions.question: Mendeleev's 1869 table ordered the elements by increasing:
questions.rationale: Mendeleev used atomic mass; Moseley's atomic-number ordering (1913) came later and fixed the anomalies.

questions.question: 'Eka-silicon', the gap Mendeleev left in his table, turned out to be:
questions.rationale: Eka-silicon became germanium (1886); eka-aluminium became gallium (1875) — both predicted with accurate masses and properties.

questions.question: The modern periodic law makes element properties a periodic function of:
questions.rationale: Moseley's X-ray work showed proton count (atomic number) is the true basis, replacing Mendeleev's atomic-mass ordering.

questions.question: Which element sits in group 2, period 3 of the periodic table?
questions.rationale: Group 2 period 3 is magnesium — an alkaline earth metal with configuration [Ne] 3s².

questions.question: Moving left to right across a period, atomic radius generally:
questions.rationale: Rising nuclear charge pulls the same shell inward, so atoms shrink across a period; they grow down a group as shells are added.

questions.question: The most electronegative element (4.0 on the Pauling scale) is:
questions.rationale: Fluorine's small size and high nuclear charge make it the strongest electron puller — 4.0, the top of the scale.

questions.question: Oxygen's first ionization energy (1314 kJ/mol) is lower than nitrogen's (1402 kJ/mol) because:
options: oxygen's fourth 2p electron must pair up, adding repulsion, while nitrogen's half-filled 2p³ is stable
questions.rationale: Pairing the fourth 2p electron in oxygen creates repulsion, making that electron easier to remove than one from nitrogen's stable half-filled shell.

questions.question: A diagonal relationship links which pair?
questions.rationale: Down-right neighbours Li–Mg, Be–Al, and B–Si share size and charge density, hence similar chemistry.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a halogen?
questions.rationale: Halogens are group 17: F, Cl, Br, I, At. Neon is a noble gas of group 18.

questions.question: The f-block inner transition elements are the:
questions.rationale: Lanthanides (Z = 58–71) and actinides (Z = 90–103) fill f orbitals and sit below the main table.
